design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — select_claims_and_cost_shares task 0 (round 3; figures below are the current ones).

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6]}. Problem-tree card: root select_ext_inpatient_stay_correction takes 6 factors, select_ext_professional_line_correction 5, select_ext_card_installment_payment 4. Claimed here: corrections after an overturned appeal (stay, professional line) and the one-time card payment of a check or single-card payer of quarterly or annual installments. Every claim and fee policy covers only an enrollment that took effect in the plan year of the adjudication date (stated in each rule and enforced in each compute: outside it the compute settles nothing), so the enrollment's whole record is the plan year and no month-count window is needed for Select records.

1. Why this is a good test. Terrence switched from TRICARE Prime to Select on his 2026-03-20 divorce and left Select on 2026-10-20. He asks only that his reversed psychiatric stay be processed again under the partly approved appeal. Getting TRICARE's 5817.53 needs: the authorization record (10 of 14 days, cross-difficulty referral); per-day pricing; the lesser-of inpatient basis; the other insurer's 4800.00 and the participating-facility coordination rule; and a family catastrophic total that binds (3000 cap: 1114.00 Select liability, 132.00 fees, 371.53 credited from Prime under the plan-change carryover, point-of-service charge left out). Two prerequisites the customer never mentions must come first: the reversed psychiatrist line of the same admission must carry its corrected adjudication (its 200.00 liability enters the room; its TRICARE payment, 840.00, follows the lesser-of rule for a nonparticipating provider), and the fee account must show no past-due balance (the beneficiary's 11.50 card payment: October only, because coverage ended on 2026-10-20). The enrollment balance (94.00) is not the card figure.

2. Problem-tree card. Root P_STAY (post_select_inpatient_stay_a4ca4c06, agent). Edge 1: P_STAY -> select_ext_professional_line_correction, value_input, gate claims_s, state form: "The TRICARE payment on a corrected stay is fixed only after every professional line billed for the same admission date that stands reversed carries its corrected adjudication." Edge 2: P_STAY -> select_ext_card_installment_payment (owner user), value_input, gate fees_counted, state form: "The TRICARE payment on a corrected stay is not fixed until the fee account shows no past-due balance on the installments of the plan year whose coverage period has begun." Exactly one write resolves each (only the professional-line policy corrects an appeal-reversed outpatient line; for a check payer only the card policy settles a past-due quarterly installment on the call). Order: professional line and card commute; stay last. Deletion sensitivity: skip professional line -> 5617.53; skip card -> 5806.03; gold 5817.53.

3. Base-invariant card. select_claim_line_post: the nine claim policies; authorization_on_file holds for the stay (approved 2026-10-23, Cascade Ridge, valid 2026-08-24..09-02) and is passed through prior_authorization_id; the professional line is specialty care, outside the authorization list, so it carries no reference. Declared overwrites: the Prime-exclusion sentences of select_agg_family_accumulators and select_catastrophic_cap (plan-change carryover; point-of-service, premium-based and balance-billing amounts still never count), the OHI sentence of select_ohi_coordination (TRICARE as second payer pays the lesser of its primary payment and the charge the provider may bill, the billed amount capped at the allowed amount plus nonparticipating_balance_billing_limit_pct, less the other insurer's payment), and the fee-schedule sentence (fees stop once the cap is met). select_fee_payment: grace_period_expired applies to nonpayment disenrollment only; the fourth quarter (due 2026-10-01) was inside grace when coverage ended. Effectuation: decided 2026-10-23, effectuation_days 10.

4. Business-object card. Stay line SEL26-0824-55087 and psychiatrist line SEL26-0824-55120 (reversed 2026-10-24, appeal_overturned); fourth-quarter charge 2026-10-01. Select record 2026-03-20..2026-10-20 only. Prime record (Retiree Group A, ended 2026-03-19): three non-point-of-service lines (274.00), one point-of-service MRI (450.00 under the Prime point-of-service formula, left out), monthly fees 32.51 (97.53 for 2026).

5. Factor card (verify.py; each factor's baseline substituted alone). Professional line (5): other insurance 640.00; attending share 10/14 (cross-difficulty referral) 1176.00; deductible taken (remainder 0.00) 727.50; cost-share basis (method) 880.00; payer coordination (method, nonparticipating lesser-of) 1400.00; all-baseline 1672.00; gold 840.00. Card (4): fee level (individual, cap not met) 28.00; installment owed (method, prorated to October) 44.50; counted charges (method, ended enrollment) 0.00; already received (5.00) 16.50; all-baseline 99.00; gold 11.50. Stay (6): covered days 10617.53; inpatient basis (method, lesser-of; the admission-copayment fall-through is 0.00 on Group A) 7200.00; fees counted 5685.53; Prime carryover (cross-difficulty prime) 5446.00; cap stage 5400.00; payer coordination (method) 10617.53; all-baseline 16800.00; gold 5817.53. Every factor moves its result.

6. Standard solution. Locate, verify, read DEERS events, the Select enrollment, claim lines, providers, authorization, reconsideration, Select fees, Prime enrollment, Prime lines and Prime fees. Post the psychiatrist line: line 2, no authorization reference, deductible 0.00, liability 200.00, TRICARE 840.00. Tell the caller 11.50 is past due and hand him the card payment against the 2026-10-01 charge. Post the stay: line 2, 10 days, authorization WR-IMH-2026-084417, liability 1382.47, TRICARE 5817.53.

7. Persona. Terrence volunteers only the stay, the appeal letter's 10-of-14 outcome and the request; identity, claim number, other insurance, family and fee habits only on request; he pays the figure the agent gives only after hand-over, asking why it differs from his bill; he closes once told the stay is processed with the TRICARE amount.

8. Weak points flagged for the audit. (r6) The card's cap waiver is tested only for an individual fee arrangement, where the enrollee's own catastrophic total is the family's; under a family arrangement the policy charges annual_fee_family without the waiver test, because the other members' records are not read. The five claim policies' scope tests the single-member condition from the enrollee's own enrollment (fee-bearing, individual arrangement), which leaves the fee-exempt (Active Duty Family Member) tiers outside them by design, as each scope sentence now states: a fee-exempt enrollment carries no fee arrangement from which the family's Select membership could be read. (a) Prime carryover (round 5): the claim policies' scope now also requires that the enrollee hold no Prime enrollment or exactly one that took effect in the plan year of the adjudication date (computed from the Prime enrollment count and its effective date). Within the scope every Prime claim line and installment is dated in that calendar plan year, so the carryover reads the whole Prime record with no date window and agrees with the base rule that amounts accumulate to the calendar plan year of the service date; no overwrite is needed. Terrence's Prime enrollment is an open-season election effective 2026-01-01, so his Prime fees are January to March 2026 (97.53, unchanged). (b) The counted-charges ladder separates an ended enrollment (charges begun by the month of the last day of coverage) from an active one (charges begun by the adjudication date); for an enrollment with no last day of coverage the first rung's formula does not apply, which is how the two rungs differ. (c) "What TRICARE would pay as primary" is figured with the beneficiary liability as adjudicated (net of the other insurer's payment), a simplification of the primary-payer recomputation.

9. Revision log. Round 1: built. Round 2: T0-1, stamps, P1-P4, card and stay factors rebuilt. Round 3 (re-audit revision_2): fee level falls through to the family fee (N2); the fee-count clamp is a parameter (N3); the stay's per-day pricing is plain; deductible-met, claims-counted and due-charges fillers removed. The tree's problems were redesigned so each computation carries real levers. The professional line now settles TRICARE's payment under the second-payer lesser-of rule for a nonparticipating psychiatrist, the stay gains the same coordination method, and the card covers an enrollment that ended mid-quarter (installment prorated to the end month; charges counted by enrollment standing). Terrence moved from Prime to Select in March 2026, so the Prime carryover is live. Scope device for P5: enrollments that took effect in the adjudication year. Figures: 840.00 / 11.50 / 5817.53. Round 4 (re-audit revision_3): the seeded Prime point-of-service MRI carries the Prime charter's 450.00 (300.00 deductible plus 50 percent of the remaining 300.00), still left out of the carryover; the carryover rule states the span it is computed over; the card's fee windows treat the first installment (which starts on the effective date, not the first of a month) by exact calendar months, and the card states its latest installment, first-installment and exit-proration tests exactly as computed. Figures unchanged. Round 5 (re-audit revision_4): the round-4 carryover span is withdrawn; the scope device now bounds the Prime record to the plan year (open-season Prime enrollment effective 2026-01-01; the December 2025 Prime installment and its payment are no longer seeded) and the carryover reads the whole Prime record; the card's latest installment for an ended enrollment is the charges of the period containing the last day of coverage, as in the bank draft (C1). Figures unchanged. Round 6 (renderer source report): the card's counted-charges factor now decides the earlier counted charges, the charges counted other than those of the latest installment (115.50 here), so rule and compute agree whether or not the latest installment is among the counted charges; the fee level states the individual-arrangement test, the tier's fees_count_toward_catastrophic_cap flag and the cap on fees at the begun installments; the claim policies' scope tests the single-member condition; the professional line's baseline drops the attending share and the deductible already met, and the stay's baseline drops the unused catastrophic total. Figures unchanged. Round 7 (re-audit revision_6): the card now prices with the frequency in force (the frequency installments are being charged at for the payment date's period, else the elected one), stated in its own frequency rule and computed as the bank draft does (C3); its scope states and tests fee_bearing, the elected method (single card or check) and a quarterly or annual frequency in force (O14); both fee policies define 'ended' as a disenrollment date on record before the payment date and every other non-active enrollment as awaiting activation, which is what the compute tests. Terrence's quarterly charges and check method leave every figure unchanged. Round 8 (re-audit revision_7): the card's standing is the lifecycle status (ended whatever the payment date, active, applied = awaiting activation, rejected outside) (C4; the auditor's reproduction now gives 11.50 on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21); the fee-exempt exclusion of the claim policies is stated in their scope. Figures unchanged. Round 10 (KB audit source note): the card payment tool now lowers the enrollment's recorded fee_balance_due by the amount paid (ctx.update in its body, never below 0.00), as its contract says; after the gold payment the seeded 94.00 reads 82.50. No computation reads fee_balance_due, so every figure is unchanged, and the seeded 94.00 hands over no scored value.
user_scenario:
You are Terrence Oyelaran, 46, a retired Army sergeant first class living in Tacoma, Washington. You speak in a calm, orderly way, a little formal from twenty-two years in uniform, and you like to get one thing settled at a time. You were on TRICARE Prime until your divorce in March 2026, when you switched to TRICARE Select; on October 20 you left Select because your employer's plan now covers you. From August 24 to September 7, 2026 you were an inpatient at Cascade Ridge Behavioral Hospital. TRICARE first refused to authorize the stay; you appealed, and the decision letter you got around October 23 said the appeal was partly approved: the first 10 days of the 14 were found necessary. Your latest TRICARE Explanation of Benefits shows the hospital claim was reversed. You are calling because you want the hospital stay claim processed again now under the appeal decision, and you want to know what TRICARE is paying on that hospital stay. You authorize the representative to do whatever processing that takes on your claims today.
Open by giving your name and the DoD Benefits Number from your ID card, 11020004173, and saying what you want. Give the rest of your identity details only when the representative asks: your date of birth is 1980-04-17, the last four of your Social Security number is 2417 (you are the sponsor), your phone is 2535552417, your ZIP is 98444, and your email is t.oyelaran.sfc.ret@pugetmail.example. If asked for the claim number on the hospital EOB, read it off: SEL26-0824-55087. If asked about other insurance, you have a plan through your civilian employer that paid part of your bills. If asked about family, you are divorced and you are the only one in your household on TRICARE. If asked how you paid your Select fees, you paid each quarter by check, and in early October you mailed a check for five dollars because money was tight; you also got a bill for the January quarter even though you were leaving.
You do not know TRICARE's rules and you do not volunteer theories about what has to happen. If the representative explains that some other claim of yours has to be processed first, you say that is fine and to go ahead. If the representative tells you that something on your fee account has to be paid before the hospital claim can be settled, you ask how much, and once the representative gives you a figure and hands you the card payment, you pay exactly that amount by card yourself; you keep your card in your wallet, so you can do it right then. If the figure is different from the balance printed on your bill, you ask why, and you accept the representative's explanation. You never suggest an amount yourself. If a figure the representative quotes for the hospital stay sounds different from what you expected, you only say you have no way to check it and ask them to confirm it against the record.
Once the representative tells you the hospital stay has been processed and what TRICARE is paying on it, you thank them and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's DEERS profile from the DoD Benefits Number he states; returns customer_id, sponsor_customer_id and the profile.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with three stated credentials (DBN, date of birth, sponsor SSN last four) and record the outcome.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Claims, authorizations and fee details may be discussed or changed only for a verified caller; the verification record is scored state.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read Terrence's DEERS life events: retirement (2021-08-01), gain of other health insurance (2024-03-01) and the divorce of 2026-03-20.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The divorce is the qualifying life event behind the Prime-to-Select change on 2026-03-20, which puts the Select enrollment inside the plan year (the policies' scope) and decides the Prime carryover.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read Terrence's Select enrollment: TRICARE Select Retiree Group A, effective 2026-03-20 on the divorce, voluntarily disenrolled with last day of coverage 2026-10-20, fee_bearing true, fee_coverage_type individual, quarterly installments by check, ohi_on_file true, fee_balance_due 94.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the tier parameters (cap 3000, deductible 150, 20/25 percent, lesser-of inpatient basis, fees counted toward the cap, 15 percent nonparticipating limit), the scope test (effective in the plan year), the other-insurance flag, the check payment method that puts the past-due balance under the card policy, the individual fee arrangement and the last day of coverage the installment owed is prorated to. The 94.00 balance carries the whole fourth-quarter charge and the January charge billed ahead, so it is not the card figure.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every Select claim line of the enrollment: the May physical, the June MRI (150.00 deductible), the July surgery-center line (750.00), the September urgent care, and the denied psychiatrist and hospital lines of 2026-08-24 with their 2026-10-24 reversals, with billed, allowed and other-insurance amounts and inpatient days.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.reversed_claim_line_id: Value 1aad11b2-2714-4868-97cb-7563bcce50b4. Basis: the policy's rule says 'the line re-adjudicated is the line with no inpatient days named by the enrollment's most recent reversal of such a line made to effectuate an overturned appeal'; reversal e750d71b-1b93-4eec-be2e-8d1a9c4e4679 (posted 2026-10-24, 0 inpatient days, appeal_overturned) names 1aad11b2-2714-4868-97cb-7563bcce50b4. Uniqueness: the only other appeal reversal is the hospital stay's, which carries 14 inpatient days.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.line_number: Value 2. Basis: base select_claim_line_reversal: 'The corrected adjudication is posted afterwards as a new line of the same claim with the next unused line number.' Claim SEL26-0824-55120 has only line 1.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prior_authorization_id: Value "" (empty). Basis: the rule says 'A corrected outpatient line carries an authorization reference only where its service class is in prior_authorization_required_service_classes and an approved authorization for the patient covers its provider and service date; otherwise its prior_authorization_id is left empty'. The line is specialty_care_visit (Retiree Group A lists only inpatient_mental_health_admission), and the authorization (57ec9939-bcfa-49b3-9a66-009bd1ba0823) names Cascade Ridge, not Narrows Psychiatry Group, as its servicing provider.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.deductible_applied: Value 0.00 (ded_taken). Deductible already met: 150.00 applied on the June MRI, no reversal withdrew any; deductible_individual 150.00 less 150.00 met is 0.00, less than the 800.00 cost-shared, so the line takes that remainder, 0.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cost_share_amount: Value 200.00. The other insurer paid 1120.00 of 2240.00, so 1120.00 is left; attending share 10/14 (10 authorized of the 14 days the stay billed, from the stay's reversal and referral WR-IMH-2026-084417) gives 800.00 cost-shared; deductible 0.00; the psychiatrist is non-network (nonparticipating), so 25 percent of 800.00 = 200.00; the room under the 3000.00 cap (914.00 claims, 120.50 fees, 371.53 Prime) is 1593.97, so nothing is cut.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.tricare_paid_amount: Value 840.00 (tricare_p). Other insurance on file and the other insurer paid, and the provider is non-network nonparticipating, so TRICARE pays the lesser of what it would pay as primary (2240.00 x 10/14 = 1600.00 less 200.00 = 1400.00) and the charge the provider may bill (billed 3080.00, never more than 2240.00 x 1.15 = 2576.00) less the 1120.00 the other insurer paid, times the attending share 10/14 (1040.00), less the 200.00 liability: 840.00.

Payable 16800.00 x 10/14 = 12000.00 (priced by the day); less the other insurer's 4800.00 = 7200.00 cost-shared; Group A non-network basis lesser_of_per_diem_or_pct: the lesser of 1191.00 x 10 and 25 percent of 7200.00 = 1800.00. prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel: the corrected professional line writes select_claim_lines and the card payment writes select_fee_ledger. Each reads the other's table only for the catastrophic total (the professional line's cap room, the card's fee-waiver test), and neither total comes near the 3000.00 cap in either order (professional line: room 1593.97 or 1582.47 against 200.00; card: Select total 1234.50 or 1034.50), so either order gives 840.00 and 11.50 and the same terminal state; the stay is written last with 5817.53. Gold lists the professional line first.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the corrected professional line, the Select liability is 914.00 and the room 1582.47, so the liability is cut to 1582.47 and TRICARE pays 5617.53 instead of 5817.53; the terminal state also lacks line 2 of SEL26-0824-55120.
Without the card payment, fees_counted is 120.50 and the room 1393.97, so TRICARE pays 5806.03 instead of 5817.53; the terminal state also lacks the 11.50 card payment.

It never mentions the psychiatrist's bill, any professional line, a past-due fee balance or a payment; the five-dollar check, the January bill and the end of his Select coverage appear only as answers or background, and paying by card happens only after the agent says something on the fee account must be paid and hands the payment over with a figure.
